units: <cite ref="Niddah 31b:50">Nidd. 31ᵇ</cite> <he>מפני מה האיש מקבל פ׳ וכ׳</he> why does man easily accept conciliatory words, and woman does not? (Answ.) This one partakes of the nature of the material of which he was created (earth being easily crushed) &c.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 2:1:14">Y. Taan. II, 65ᵇ</cite> bot. <he>ואני מקבל פִּיּוּסָן</he> and I shall accept their apology.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 93:6">Gen. R. s. 93</cite> <he>הגשה לפ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="E00093"><he>הַגָּשָׁה</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 93:9">Ib.</cite> <he>כל הדברים … היה בהם פ׳ ליוסף וכ׳</he> all the words … (<cite ref="Genesis 44:18-34">Gen. XLIV, 18—34</cite>) contained conciliatory argument for Joseph, for his brothers, and for Benjamin.

<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 7:2:1">Koh. R. to VII, 2</cite> <he>מדה שיש בה פ׳</he> a social act with which consolation is connected; a. fr.—Pl. <cite ref="Q00687"><he>פִּיּוּסִים</he></cite>, <cite ref="Q01464"><he>פִּיּוּסִין</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 74:10">Gen. R. s. 74</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Genesis 31:36">Gen. XXXI, 36</cite>) <he>דא את סבור … דברי פ׳ וכ׳</he> here you might think there would be blows and wounds, but (his anger found vent only in) words of persuasion &c.; a. e.—[<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 26:4">Lev. R. s. 26</cite> <he>בפיוסין</he>, read: <he>בפִיסְטִין</he>.]
